items.summary_orig: Customers rarely pay everything at once. A customer pays half today and the rest next week; a supplier gets a deposit now and the balance after delivery. If your sheet only records "paid" or "not paid", those in-between amounts disappear — and month-end totals quietly go wrong. The fix is three columns per item: Amount, Paid, Remaining.

items.title_orig: What makes rock deep beneath continents break away and sink?

items.summary_orig: We usually picture mountain building as rock being pushed upward. items.title: 如何用预签名 URL 与保留策略上传 AI 生成图像
items.title_orig: How to Upload AI-Generated Images with Presigned URLs and Retention Policies
items.summary: 在服务端生成短期预签名 URL 交给 worker 或浏览器，再以 HTTP PUT 上传，访问密钥始终留在服务端。
items.summary_orig: TL;DR: Generate a short-lived presigned URL on your server, send only that URL to the worker or browser, then upload the image with an HTTP PUT . The access key stays server-side. For a training-artifact pipeline, the harder decision is not the upload. It is deciding when an object may be deleted, and whether the storage system can prove that decision later.

items.title: 神经网络为何自信却出错，以及如何校准
items.title_orig: Calibration: Why Neural Networks Are Confident and Wrong - and How to Fix Them
items.summary: 校准良好的分类器说 90% 确信就应约 90% 正确，但现代神经网络常严重偏离这一标准。
items.summary_orig: A classifier that says it is 90% sure should be right about 90% of the time. That sounds like a low bar, and yet most modern neural networks fail it badly. They are routinely 99% confident and wrong, or 60% confident and right almost every time. Their accuracy can be excellent while their confidence is meaningless.
